label: copy phase: just copied z (input z), now outputting z or b, from recall position 3 onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is z (the model just emitted z; 99.98% of activations), and almost always when the token being output now is z (55% of mass) or b (39%), i.e. the original sequence has z followed by z or b. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, never on recall positions 0-1 and rarely on 2, and not when the input is any token other than z. Input z followed by other outputs (s, p, f, ...) gets weak low-quartile activations that make up most of the misses. Largest activations: z-z or z-b pairs at recall index 3-5, often in sequences with repeated z (in_count >= 2 raises the rate). Inside a run of z the second z fires more weakly than the first. Dev F1 0.865, mass recall 0.94.

issues: The scores reproduce exactly. Test precision 0.908, recall 0.832, F1 0.869, mass recall 0.941.

The structural claims hold. The feature never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter (0 active of 3.7M dev steps). In the copy phase, in_tok==z covers 99.95% of test activations (mass recall 0.99998). Recall indices 0 and 1 never fire. At recall_idx==2, z followed by z or b has precision of only 0.067, against 0.91 at recall_idx 3 and 0.98 at recall_idx 4.

The misses on the test split are what the explanation describes: input z followed by some other output (s, p, f, e, ...), all at low activation (about 0.02-0.36 of max). Together they hold 5.9% of the mass. Adding s to the output set lowers F1 to 0.731, so these misses cannot be picked up cheaply.

The false positives (357 on test) are spread across positions. Precision for z-to-b is 0.86 and for z-to-z is 0.96. At recall_idx>=6 precision is 0.81 and at to_go==0 it is 0.87. These are mild drops, not a separate class. Excluding late final steps lowers F1 to 0.823.
The magnitude claim 'in_count>=2 raises firing' checks out: precision 0.944 for in_count>=2 vs 0.859 for in_count==1, and the mean per-hit activation is higher.
The magnitude claim 'peaks at recall index 3 to 5' checks out: precision 0.949 at recall_idx<=5 vs 0.806 at >=6, and the mean activation is higher.

The claim 'inside a run of z, the second z fires more weakly than the first' is NOT supported. With prev_tok==z, mass recall divided by recall is 1.14. With prev_tok!=z it is 1.13. Mean activation is about the same, and runs are rare (129 predicted steps). This is a minor overclaim in the explanation; the label and predicate are fine.
